steps: High-flow oxygen to SpO2 94-98%; back-to-back nebulised salbutamol (+ ipratropium if severe).
Oral prednisolone 40-50 mg (or IV hydrocortisone) early.
IV magnesium sulfate for severe/life-threatening attacks.
Reassess with PEF/ABG; escalate to ICU for exhaustion, rising CO2 or silent chest.
Identify trigger; review inhaler technique/adherence and step-up preventer at discharge.

drugRefs.freq: repeat every 15-20 min / back-to-back in severe attacks
drugRefs.why: First-line bronchodilator — relaxes airway smooth muscle to reverse bronchospasm.
Added to salbutamol in acute severe/life-threatening asthma for additional bronchodilation.
Reduces airway inflammation and prevents relapse; give as early as possible.
Alternative to oral prednisolone when the patient cannot swallow/absorb oral steroid.
Bronchodilator for severe/life-threatening attacks not responding to initial nebulised therapy.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Asthma
Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) — Management of Exacerbations
BTS/SIGN British Guideline on the Management of Asthma

confirm: Acute wheeze/dyspnoea/cough with reduced PEF; grade severity (PEF, SpO2, ability to speak, silent chest).
disposition: Admit if not responding; ICU if life-threatening.
